name: Chat Skin over PTY ("Peau de chat") — incremental hybrid via rollout-JSONL mirroring
coreIdea: Keep the existing PTY/xterm pipeline untouched as the execution engine: Codex CLI keeps running as a full TUI inside the shell PTY exactly as today. Add a per-session chat surface that is a read-model over the session's rollout JSONL file (the structured transcript Codex already writes under CODEX_HOME/sessions/...), not a parser of ANSI bytes. Input goes IN through the existing write_terminal/sendLine path (same mechanism the Skill buttons use today); output comes OUT by tailing the rollout file through an extension of the existing discussions.rs module. Each TerminalSession gets a two-position toggle — "Chat" (default, primary surface) and "Terminal" (the raw xterm, always one click away) — both views of the same PTY + same Codex session. No new Codex launch mode, no app-server dependency, no framework migration: the chat panel is built with the exact targeted-innerHTML + poll + scroll-preservation pattern the Agent Room already uses (renderRoomFeedInner/#roomFeed/refreshRoom in src/main.ts). This is the lowest-risk path: if anything in chat fails (JSONL claim race, unknown event type, Codex login prompt), the session silently remains fully operable in the raw terminal.
architecture: INPUT PATH (unchanged engine): user types in the new #chatComposer (rendered by a new renderChatPanel() in src/main.ts, modeled on renderRoomPanel() L1253) → submit calls the existing sendLine() (src/main.ts L4689) → invoke("write_terminal", {id, data+"\r"}) through src/platform.ts (Tauri IPC on desktop; WS {type:"input"} frame or POST /api/terminals/:id/write in remote mode) → src-tauri/src/terminal.rs writes into the PTY where the Codex TUI is running. The composer also flips the session into "awaiting" state and stashes the sent text as an optimistic user bubble. OUTPUT PATH (new read-model, reusing discussions.rs): Codex CLI appends structured events to its rollout JSONL (CODEX_HOME/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-<ts>-<uuid>.jsonl). The session↔file binding already exists: claimSessionForTerminal (src/main.ts L676) → claim_session_for_terminal (src-tauri/src/discussions.rs L420) yields codexSessionId stored on TerminalSession and persisted in localStorage. Two NEW backend commands in discussions.rs, registered in src-tauri/src/lib.rs and mirrored as REST routes in src-tauri/src/server.rs + cases in platform.ts remoteInvoke(): (1) get_discussion_transcript{accountId, sessionId} — resolves the HEAD fork file via find_rollout_by_id (L1037) + collapse_forks (L350) semantics, then parses the whole file with the established contains-then-serde pattern into a typed ChatItem[] (userMessage, agentMessage, reasoning?, commandExecution?, tokenCount, turnContext, unknown→generic "activity" item; is_synthetic_prompt filtering reused); returns items + byteOffset. (2) read_transcript_delta{filePath, byteOffset} — reads only appended complete lines from byteOffset (partial trailing line held back), returns new ChatItems + new offset; O(delta), no rescans. FRONTEND LOOP: while a chat view is active, a poll (900ms when awaiting a turn, 5s idle — same lifecycle slot as the other per-view intervals in setActiveView L1418) calls read_transcript_delta and patches ONLY #chatFeed via targeted innerHTML swap with the atBottom auto-scroll preservation copied from refreshRoom (L1326-1330); the composer lives outside the swapped node so focus/draft survive; full render() rebuilds re-mount the chat panel like any other view. Turn state: a turn is "running" from prompt send until a token_count event arrives after the echoed user_message; agent_message items appearing before that render progressively. Rendering: escape-first (escapeHtml) then a small whitelist markdown subset (fences, inline code, bold, links) implemented in a new src/chat-render.ts — no third-party markdown/sanitizer lib, preserving the file's escape-everything convention. Meanwhile the raw pty-data → xterm.write path in setupEvents (L4745) keeps running for the SAME session, so the detached xterm instance (mountActiveTerminal pattern L4521) stays hot and the Terminal toggle is instant with full history.
phases: PHASE 1 — Backend transcript API (files: src-tauri/src/discussions.rs, src-tauri/src/lib.rs, src-tauri/src/server.rs, src/platform.ts). Add ChatItem enum + parser reusing parse_rollout_filename/find_rollout_by_id/collapse_forks/is_synthetic_prompt and the contains-prefilter-then-serde pattern; commands get_discussion_transcript and read_transcript_delta; register in lib.rs invoke_handler; add GET /api/discussions/transcript and /api/discussions/transcript-delta with auth_or in server.rs; add both cases to remoteInvoke() switch in platform.ts. ACCEPTANCE: invoking get_discussion_transcript on an existing discussion returns ordered user/agent messages matching what `codex resume` shows, in BOTH desktop and remote modes; delta call after a live turn returns only the new lines; unknown event types come back as {kind:'unknown', rawType} without erroring; partial trailing JSONL lines never produce a corrupt item.

PHASE 2 — Chat view skeleton + toggle (files: src/main.ts, src/style.css). Add per-session surface mode ('chat'|'terminal') on TerminalSession (default 'terminal' for now); renderChatPanel() cloned from renderRoomPanel() (#chatFeed + #chatComposer + per-session header chip); toggle button in header.topbar .actions and on the session row; bindUi() wiring + createIcons() after every swap; composer submit → optimistic user bubble → sendLine(); initial load via get_discussion_transcript keyed on session.codexSessionId; poll loop started/stopped alongside the view like existing intervals; chat CSS appended AFTER the Event Horizon layer (style.css line ~3745) consuming --panel/--line/--text/--accent/--radius tokens; French labels ('Conversation', 'Envoyer', 'Basculer vers le terminal'). ACCEPTANCE: send a prompt from the composer and watch the reply appear as bubbles without opening xterm; toggling to Terminal shows the same live session (xterm never disposed); toggling back restores chat scroll position; composer draft and focus survive a full render() (e.g. triggered by pool poll).

PHASE 3 — Live tail, turn states, resilience (files: src/main.ts, src-tauri/src/discussions.rs). Byte-offset delta polling at 900ms while turn running / 5s idle; 'Codex réfléchit…' indicator between prompt send and terminating token_count; dedupe optimistic user bubble against the echoed user_message; graceful degradation: if codexSessionId is still null (claim retries up to ~28s can fail), chat shows a 'liaison de session en cours…' banner and the toggle defaults to Terminal; on pty-exit mark the conversation ended; unknown/unparsed events render as collapsed activity chips with a 'voir le terminal' hint. ACCEPTANCE: during a long multi-minute Codex turn the feed updates within ~1s cadence and never duplicates messages across delta calls; killing and resuming the session (codex resume flow, buildResumeCommand L661) reattaches chat to the HEAD fork file with full prior history; claim failure leaves a fully working terminal session with a visible notice.

PHASE 4 — Rendering polish + cards (files: src/chat-render.ts NEW, src/main.ts, src/style.css, src-tauri/src/discussions.rs). Escape-first markdown subset (fences with copy button, inline code, bold, links); reverse-engineer additional rollout event types from real files (exec/command, file-change, reasoning) and add card renderers, keeping the unknown-type fallback; per-session header chips: model (turn_context), cumulative tokens + cost (token_count + metrics::cost_for_usage pattern from account_usage.rs). ACCEPTANCE: code fences render monospaced with working copy; adversarial content (user prompt containing or ``````) never executes or breaks layout (manual XSS pass); a session that ran shell commands shows them as collapsed cards.

PHASE 5 — Chat as primary surface + history integration (files: src/main.ts, src-tauri/src/settings.rs, src/style.css). AppSettings gains chatPrimary (default true, round-tripped through save_settings/readSettingsForm L4420); new sessions open on the chat surface once codexSessionId is claimed (auto-flip from a brief terminal/claiming state); Discussions view rows gain 'Ouvrir en chat' → read-only transcript view with a 'Reprendre' button that starts a resume terminal and binds chat to it (reusing resumeSessionInTerminal L1643); sidebar session list shows last-message preview from the transcript instead of only the account label. ACCEPTANCE: fresh session lands in chat within seconds of launch with the Codex greeting turn visible; chatPrimary=false restores today's exact behavior; opening an old discussion renders its full transcript without starting a PTY; README/screenshot note updated.
keepsRawTerminal: Fully. The PTY/xterm pipeline is not modified at all — pty-data still feeds every session's xterm instance (detached-but-alive per the existing mountActiveTerminal pattern), so the Terminal toggle on each session and in the topbar switches instantly to the raw TUI with complete scrollback. The terminal remains the mandatory escape hatch for: Codex login/device-auth flows, approval prompts if an account has bypass=false, agent status/doctor subcommands, and any event the JSONL parser doesn't understand (chat shows a 'voir le terminal' chip in those cases). chatPrimary=false in settings restores today's terminal-first behavior wholesale, and any session whose rollout file cannot be claimed automatically stays terminal-only.
risks: Rollout JSONL is written asynchronously by Codex CLI: chat lags the TUI by up to a flush interval, and agent_message items may appear only at turn boundaries on some Codex versions — mid-turn streaming granularity is NOT guaranteed (this is the structural ceiling of the hybrid; the app-server path lifts it later).

Rollout event schema is undocumented and version-drifting: only session_meta/user_message/agent_message/token_count/turn_context are known to the codebase today; new Codex releases may rename fields. Mitigated by the unknown→activity-chip fallback and contains-prefilter parsing, but card fidelity will trail Codex updates.

Session↔file binding inherits the claim_session_for_terminal race (filename-timestamp heuristic, up to ~28s retries, can mis-pair with multiple simultaneous terminals on one account); chat must tolerate null/late/wrong codexSessionId — wrong pairing would show another session's transcript (mitigate by verifying the first user_message matches a sent prompt).

Prompts injected via write_terminal while the Codex TUI is mid-redraw can interleave (existing Skill-button risk, now on the primary path); need a busy guard (queue sends while a turn is running) or accept occasional garbled TUI input.

Turn-completion detection is heuristic (token_count after echoed user_message); pathological turns (errors, interrupts via terminal Ctrl+C) can leave the 'thinking' indicator stuck — needs a timeout + terminal-toggle hint.
Fork/resume semantics: transcripts must always read the HEAD fork (collapse_forks assumption message_count=max); a fork from an earlier point would silently truncate history.

Full innerHTML render() can still nuke chat DOM if the panel isn't strictly patched via targeted #chatFeed swaps — every new global re-render trigger added later is a regression hazard for composer focus/scroll.

Dual-mode parity tax: the two new commands must land in lib.rs AND server.rs AND platform.ts together or web mode silently degrades; remote mode also reads JSONL on the server's disk (fine — CODEX_HOME lives server-side there) but multi-node routing means the transcript route must target the node that owns the terminal (route via remoteTerminalRoutes like write_terminal does).
Hand-rolled markdown subset carries XSS responsibility; scope must stay tiny (escape-first, whitelist transforms only) and be regression-tested with hostile transcripts.

main.ts is already 4889 lines with ~40 mutable globals and uncommitted feat/agent-room changes; adding ~600-800 more lines increases entropy — put the parser/renderer in new files (src/chat-render.ts) and coordinate with the in-flight branch before starting.
effortEstimate: Roughly 2.5-3.5 developer-weeks total for one developer familiar with the repo. Phase 1 (Rust transcript API + dual-mode plumbing): 3-4 days. Phase 2 (chat panel + toggle): 2-3 days — an MVP demo (chat over a live session, both directions) exists at end of week 1.5. Phase 3 (tailing/turn-state robustness): 2-3 days. Phase 4 (markdown + event cards + XSS pass): 3-4 days, dominated by reverse-engineering real rollout event types. Phase 5 (primary-surface flip + discussions integration): 2 days. No new dependencies, no Codex version requirement beyond what already writes rollouts, fully reversible via the chatPrimary setting.
